newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MOLITOR GETS 3,000TH HIT BUT TWINS FALL TO ROYALS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MOLITOR GETS 3,000TH HIT BUT TWINS FALL TO ROYALS.

text.p: Paul Molitor became the 21st player in major-league history to reach 3,000 hits Monday but his Minnesota Twins fell to the Kansas City Royals 6-5.
"It was a very special moment in what has been a long career and one that has been appreciated," said the Twins' 40-year-old designated hitter about reaching the milestone.

Molitor singled in the first inning for hit number 2,999 and then with one out in the fifth, after fouling his first pitch off, ripped a line drive to the gap in right-centre off Royals rookie left-hander Jose Rosado, who was just three years old when Molitor made his major-league debut in 1978.
The ball appeared to be playable by right fielder Jon Nunnally, but he was called off by rookie centre fielder Roderick Myers, who could not make the catch.
"I think the only time I took my eye off the ball was to make sure I touched first," Molitor said. "I did not hit the ball well. It was a fastball up.
"You could see they were coming together. The right fielder pulled up a little. I saw the ball hit the turf. I smelled triple and your instinct takes over."

The sparse crowd of 16,843 at Kauffman Stadium began a standing ovation that lasted nearly three minutes. During the ovation, Molitor saluted the crowd and exchanged hugs with teammates and manager Tom Kelly. Molitor blew a kiss to his wife and daughter as a video tribute played on the scoreboard.

Molitor also acknowledged Robin Yount, his former longtime teammate with the Milwaukee Brewers and a member of the 3,000-hit club who was in attendance. "I cannot express enough gratitude to Robin Yount for coming," he said.

"I reminded myself every day that this is something you enjoy and not fight," said Molitor, a hometown Minnesota favourite and native of St. Paul. "You do feel a sense of relief once you reach that level."
The historic hit came three years to the day after Dave Winfield got his 3,000th, also with the Twins. It marked the first time a player reached the plateau with a triple.

Molitor finished the night 3-for-5 with an RBI. He has 3,001 career hits and passed Roberto Clemente and Cap Anson for 19th place on the all-time list. He is six hits short of tying former Tiger Al Kaline for 18th place.
Chuck Knoblauch got his 1,000th hit and Pat Meares homered for Minnesota, but Keith Lockhart's two-run homer keyed a five-run sixth inning that lifted the Royals past Minnesota.
In Toronto, Tim Raines hit a pair of three-run homers on his 37th birthday and Jimmy Key pitched eight scoreless innings as the New York Yankees routed the Blue Jays 10-0.

The American League East-leading Yankees went 6-1 on their seven-game road trip and moved three games ahead of the Orioles, who were idled Monday when rain in Baltimore washed out their scheduled game with the Milwaukee Brewers.
New York hosts Baltimore in a three-game series starting Tuesday and has a magic number of seven for clinching its second straight post-season appearance.

Key (12-10) allowed two hits and struck out four against his former club. He has won three straight decisions and retired the first 17 batters of the game before Tomas Perez singled past second baseman Mariano Duncan into right field with two out in the sixth.
"I just misplayed that ball," said Duncan.
Toronto starter Paul Quantrill (5-14) was tagged for seven runs and six hits in five innings.

Raines snapped an 0-for-12 slump with three-run shots in the third and fifth innings. Ruben Rivera also homered for New York. Third baseman Wade Boggs, sidelined for more than a week with back problems, walked three times and scored twice.
In Chicago, Jack McDowell tossed a nine-hitter against his former club and Kevin Seitzer added a clutch two-run single in the sixth as the Cleveland Indians beat the White Sox 4-3.
The Indians can clinch their second straight American League Central title with a victory Tuesday over the fading White Sox, who fell three games behind the Orioles in the wild-card race.

McDowell (12-9) struck out five without a walk in his fifth complete game of the season. Chicago starter Wilson Alvarez (15-9), winless in his last three starts, had his streak of 20 scoreless innings against the Indians snapped.
Frank Thomas, who hit three homers Sunday, had three hits including his 36th homer. Harold Baines also homered for Chicago.
In Seattle, Jamie Moyer scattered four hits over eight innings and Dave Hollins singled home two runs in a three-run fifth inning as the Mariners shut out the Texas Rangers 6-0.
Moyer (12-3) walked two and struck out five. Bobby Ayala pitched a perfect ninth.
Seattle has won five straight and cut the Rangers' lead to five games in the A.L. West with three games left between the teams. Seattle has won seven of the 10 meetings.
